name: Masons Falls

facts.claim: Waterfall and picnic area in Kinglake National Park near Kinglake West, 65 km north-east of Melbourne
A short walk leads to water cascading over sheer mudstone walls, fossilised sea beds
Picnic shelters among tall eucalypts; the site's BBQs are currently listed as closed

access_note: Parks Victoria page shows an "area is closed" banner and closed BBQs; check status before visiting. Parks Victoria page lists no entry fee; Kinglake NP is free to enter.

name: Wombelano Falls

facts.claim: Waterfall in Kinglake National Park reached by a 1.5 km circuit through tall eucalypt forest and fern gullies
A lookout views the falls cascading 90 metres into the gully below
Forest is regenerating after the 2009 Black Saturday bushfires

access_note: Parks Victoria page shows an "area is closed" banner; last 300 m of Captains Creek Road is unsurfaced; no dogs.

facts.claim: Artists' community in Eltham, Melbourne, established by Justus Jorgensen in 1934 on five hectares of gardens
Dozens of buildings including houses, halls, studios, galleries and stables built from recycled materials
Described as Australia's oldest continuous artist community; adult admission includes current exhibitions; cafe and winebar on site

name: Mount Leura

facts.claim: 313 m scoria cone with a dry crater 100 m deep, an extinct volcano near Camperdown
A 1932 road allows vehicles up to the summit lookout
On a clear day the lookout sees the Grampians, Mount Buninyong and the crater lakes Bullen-Merri and Gnotuk

access_note: Summit road closes during hillclimb events

facts.claim: 96 heritage-listed bathing boxes extend over 500 m of beachfront along Dendy Street Beach, Brighton
Most were built between 1907 and 1933 and added to the Victorian Heritage Register in 2018
Street in the Melbourne suburb of St Kilda, popular for its many restaurants and proximity to St Kilda beach
Historically a centre of Melbourne's Jewish community, with European-style cake shops
